text.p: Mexico annoucned sweeping changes to their squad for this month's World Cup qualifying match with Jamaica, after their shock defeat to Honduras ten days ago.

Coach Bora Milutinovic, who could lose his job if Mexico fail to win the game in CONCACAF semi-final stage group three, made eight changes to the squad. They included the recall of veteran midfielders Marcelino Bernal and Benjamin Galindo and Brazilian-born striker Zague.
Striker Carlos Hermosillo, chosen for the Honduras game after being left out for years, kept his place.
Mexico beat St. Vincent away but then lost 2-1 to Honduras while Jamaica have won their opening two games, at home to Honduras and away to St. Vincent.
The top two teams in the group progress to the six-team final round of the CONCACAF qualifying tournament. Squad:
Goalkeepers - Jorge Campos (Galaxy-United States), Oswaldo Sanchez (America), Adolfo Rios (Veracruz)
Defenders - Pavel Pardo (Atlas), Claudio Suarez (Guadalajara), German Villa (America), Francisco Gomez (UNL), Duilio Davino (UAG), Joel Sanchez (Guadalajara)

Midfielders - Ramon Ramirez (Guadalajara), Alberto Garcia Aspe (Necaxa), Jose Manuel Abundis (Toluca), Alberto Coyote (Guadalajara), Marcelino Bernal (Toluca), Raul Rodrigo Lara (America), Benjamin Galindo (Santos)
Forwards - Ricardo Peleaz (Necaxa), Damian Alvarez (Leon), Luis Garcia (America), Carlos Hermosillo (Cruz Azul), Enrique Alfaro (Toluca), Zague (Atlante)
